slides.title: Deniz Construction Management System

content.text: Mbarara University of Science and Technology

notes: Speaker 1 | 30 seconds. Introduce the client, a construction materials business that produces blocks, pavers and kerbs. State that this is Group K’s requirements engineering project.

Rehearsal plan. 14 minutes of content, 1 minute for handoffs and about 5 minutes of Q&A. Assign the ten speaking slots using members’ actual contributions. Each member should prepare one sentence about their own work and one question they can answer.
Source. Groups Presentation Guide for SWE2102, 10 November 2026.

Source. Original Group K presentation JSON.

slides.title: Problem and project scope

content.heading: One primary operator
content.text: The Sales Manager handles sales, records and cash reconciliation. The Owner reviews the daily report.

content.heading: During the day
content.text: Record sales, update stock and print receipts while customers collect their purchases.

content.heading: At the end of the day
content.text: Record expenses, compare expected cash with the physical count and save the daily report.

notes: Speaker 2 | 2 minutes. Explain why the Sales Manager is the primary user and why the Owner needs a finalized report. Deniz takes payment upfront. The group observed daytime receipting and learned that the Sales Manager uses the laptop to process deficits.
Q&A prompt. Why design two workflows? Daytime receipting has to happen at the sale, while checking cash and saving the daily report happens at close.
Sources. Phase 1 Elicitation and Stakeholder Analysis, sections 2 and 5. Master specification, Part 1 scope and REC requirements.

Technical Q&A. Each sale can have multiple product lines. The Sales_Items trigger deducts stock from Products. If any line is oversold, the whole sale rolls back. The receipt prints after commit. The database design retains original receipts and records voids or refunds as linked adjustments.

slides.title: Stakeholders and elicitation methods

content.heading: Stakeholders
content.text: Sales Manager and Owner. Workers and customers are affected. URA is the external regulator.

content.heading: Direct observation
content.text: We saw the laptop in use and receipts being printed as trucks loaded.

content.heading: Semi-structured interview
content.text: The Sales Manager reported upfront payments by cash, Mobile Money or bank deposit.

notes: Speaker 3 | 1 minute. Distinguish the primary operator, the report audience and the affected stakeholders. The Sales Manager was interviewed during the single site visit. The Owner and workers were unavailable for interviews.
Speaker 4 | 1 minute. Explain what each method contributed. Observation showed the timing of receipting. The interview provided payment rules that were not visible from truck loading alone.
Q&A prompt. Why combine observation with an interview? Each answered a different question about how the work is done.
Source. Phase 1 Elicitation and Stakeholder Analysis, sections 4 to 6.

slides.title: Group K’s elicitation example

content.heading: Observation
content.text: Receipts were printed while customers’ trucks were being loaded.

content.heading: Limitation
content.text: We could see receipts being printed but could not inspect the fields on them.

content.heading: Design decision
content.text: Print a receipt when the sale is saved. Specify the receipt fields separately.

notes: Speaker 5 | 2 minutes. Explain the difference between timing and content. Seeing a receipt printed supports immediate receipting. It does not establish what the existing receipt contains. We recorded that gap because a follow-up visit was not feasible.
Q&A prompt. What did the receipt observation change? It gave us evidence that recording sales and printing receipts had to be supported during the day.
Sources. Phase 1 Elicitation and Stakeholder Analysis, sections 5 and 6. Master specification, REQ-FUN-SAL-04.

slides.title: Key requirements and the offline check

content.heading: Post sales and print receipts
content.text: Give customers a receipt while their truck is being loaded.

content.heading: Log each cash expense
content.text: Account for cash paid out on the selected business date.

content.heading: Reconcile and close the day
content.text: Compare the cash count with expected cash and save the final report for the Owner.

content.heading: Offline resilience (REQ-NFR-PER-01)
content.text: Disconnect the laptop, post a sale and print its receipt. Check that the sale is stored locally.

notes: Speaker 6 | 1.5 minutes. Explain the three functional examples and the person each helps. Sale entry and printing are REQ-FUN-SAL-01 and REQ-FUN-SAL-04. Expense logging is REQ-FUN-REC-02. Cash variance and closing are REQ-FUN-REC-04 and REQ-FUN-REC-05.
Speaker 7 | 1.5 minutes. Explain why the system should handle a sale without internet. Present the disconnect, save, print and local storage sequence as a planned pass check.
Q&A prompt. What makes the NFR measurable? The test has a defined offline condition and observable outcomes for posting, printing and local storage.
Source. Master specification, Part 1 functional and non-functional requirements.

Traceability reference for Q&A. The master contains the full matrix. These are the 19 requirement mappings.
REQ-FUN-REC-02 | Operational Expense Logging | Operational_Expenses linked to Business_Day
REQ-FUN-REC-03 | Expected Cash Computation | Daily_Payment_Activity and Business_Day opening cash, less Operational_Expenses
REQ-FUN-REC-04 | Variance Reporting with Mandatory Explanation | Daily_Reconciliation table with Variance and Explanation columns
REQ-FUN-REC-01 | Daily Payment Activity by Channel | Daily_Payment_Activity grouped by business date and payment method
REQ-FUN-SAL-01 | Transactional Sale Entry | Sales and Sales_Items posted in one transaction
REQ-FUN-REC-05 | Daily Summary Report Generation | CloseDay and the saved Daily_Reconciliation report
REQ-FUN-SAL-02 | Automated VAT Calculation | CalculateVAT stored procedure (Subtotal * 0.18)
REQ-FUN-SAL-03 | Sequential Receipts and Sale Adjustments | Sales and Sale_Adjustments preserve the original receipt and correction history
REQ-FUN-SAL-04 | Physical Receipt Printing | Application prints after the sale transaction commits
REQ-FUN-SAL-05 | Inventory Deduction Trigger | AFTER INSERT on Sales_Items updates Products.Current_Stock
REQ-FUN-ATT-01 | Worker Attendance Logging with Unique Daily Constraint | Attendance table with PK (Worker_ID, Date)
REQ-FUN-ATT-02 | Daily Payroll Eligibility | Payroll_Eligibility view joining Workers and Attendance
REQ-FUN-TAX-01 | URA Summary Report | URA_Summary shows recorded VAT and separate adjustments
REQ-FUN-BAK-01 | Automated Nightly Backup | Backup job scheduled after evening reconciliation
REQ-NFR-SEC-01 | Role Based Access Control | Database roles and restricted views
REQ-NFR-SEC-02 | Immutable Audit Trail | Audit_Log table with insert only semantics
REQ-NFR-USR-01 | Low Literacy Interface | UI with icons and minimal text
REQ-NFR-PER-01 | Offline Resilience | Local database with queued sync
REQ-NFR-PER-02 | Hardware Compatibility | Optimized queries and indexing

slides.title: Close of Day prototype

content.text: Close of Day screenshot to be added
content.caption: Prototype with sample data

notes: Before presenting, insert one large screenshot of the actual Close of Day prototype. Use sample data. Keep the business date, three payment-channel totals, expected and actual cash, variance and explanation visible.
Speaker 8 | 1.5 minutes. Point to the business date and the separate recorded activity for Cash, Mobile Money and Bank Deposit. Explain that the three totals belong to the selected date.

Speaker 9 | 1.5 minutes. Walk through the sample from the verification plan. UGX 450,000 expected, UGX 445,000 counted and a UGX 5,000 deficit. A nonzero variance requires an explanation. Reflect on why separating two business dates matters. Closing one day must preserve its report without clearing or mixing activity for another date.
Q&A prompt. Why save the close by date? The Owner needs to reopen the same finalized report, and a second close must return the saved result.
Source. Master specification, REQ-FUN-REC-01 through REQ-FUN-REC-05 and Part 3 verification cases. Figures are sample data.

Technical Q&A. Opening cash, net cash activity and logged expenses determine expected cash for the business date. CloseDay locks that date, saves the report snapshot and marks the date closed in the same transaction. Daily_Payment_Activity groups recorded activity by date and payment channel. URA_Summary shows recorded VAT and adjustments separately.

slides.title: What we learned

content.heading: Fieldwork shaped the design
content.text: Seeing when receipts were printed showed us when the system needed to record sales.

content.heading: The prototype shows the proposed workflow
content.text: The next checks are offline sales and printing, and a close that preserves each business date.

notes: Speaker 10 | 1 minute. Recap what Group K observed, the requirement it produced and what still needs verification. Invite questions.

Individual Q&A | About 5 minutes. Each person should be able to state their own contribution and explain one project decision, requirement or course concept. Use the prompts on the previous slides to rehearse.
Sources. Phase 1 field observations and master specification verification plan.
